To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the self-regulating fine tunability of the MACP cavity, through the conformational change of its macrocyclic ring, is the main factor that enables it to form various types of molecular complexes with different geometries with diols.
the conformational change in the host molecule is induced by the formation of a hydrogen-bonded complex with the guest, which is a unique phenomenon in the field of molecular recognition.
a highly selective recognition of diol guests by MACP-4 was accomplished in solution and the crystalline solid state.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of novel synthetic strategies and the discovery of new host molecules that are capable of self-regulation of the host conformation in order to form the most stable host-guest complexes with a variety of guest species.

the design of a new class of self-regulating host molecules, MACP-2 and MACP-4, which can undergo conformational inversion very rapidly in solution to form a cavity of the appropriate size and geometry to best fit the guest molecules through the intermolecular hydrogen bond, C-H...Pi, and pi-pig interactions with the host molecules.

the development of new molecular hosts with a self-regulating cavity size and shape that can be fine-tuned to best match the guest species, which is a prerequisite for highly selective recognition of the guests.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

MACP-4 can self-regulate the formation of a fine-tunable cavity to recognize the guest species through a variety of intermolecular noncovalent interactions, and thus form a variety of molecular-sandwic...
MACP-4 is capable of forming a highly selective molecular sandwich complex with resorcinal and a 1:2 molecular capsule with 1,4-butanediol and 1,4-pentanediol.

MACP-4 can recognize diols in a selective and highly specific manner by forming different types of host-guest complexes depending upon the size and geometry of the guests, and by undergoing self-regulated conformational inversion in solution.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the host-guest interaction between the host (MACP-1) and guest (resorcinol) molecules in the solid state is more favorable than in solution owing to the favorable entropic effect of the host-guest complex formation.

MACP-4 can recognize the diol structure in solution and in the solid state through a self-regulation mechanism, and that the recognition ability is highly selective and dependent upon the guest species and their concentration.

a fine-tunable cavity of MACP-4 can be self-regulated to form a cavity of the best size and shape to fit the guest species, and that a guest species can also be used to control the conformation of the host molecule, thus leading to the formation of the most stable host-guest complex.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the dynamic conformational inversion process of the MACP macrocycle is self-regulated by the host-guest interactions to maximize the host-guest binding energy, thus resulting in the formation of the most stable host-guest complexes.
the self-regulated fine-tuning of the host conformation by the guest species can provide a new paradigm for the development of molecular receptors with enhanced selectivity.
the self-regulation of the host structure by guest species can be used to fine-tune the host cavity size to best fit the guest species and to form a more stable host-guest complex.
